reasoning: For the organ Palestinians do say il-kabid, with a helping vowel in the cluster. For liver as food the word is kibde, كبدة, with taa marbuta.
The loan bus is spelled with ص and is genuinely emphatic, so baaS. م is a moon letter and the taa marbuta after س is e.
Form II with shadda on خ, so the digraph kh is written twice.
A European borrowing in the political register, where the ق is usually kept as q rather than glottalised. ط is emphatic T and the ending is -iyye.
Form II from bhaar or tawaabil, with shadda on ب. Ordinary kitchen verb.
mumkin plus the bare imperfect is the normal request. The initial hamza seat is just a, then ق is a glottal stop: a'3ud. Long oo in hoon.
biddi with shadda on د is the Palestinian want. The quadriliteral faDfaD, to pour one's heart out, takes both emphatic D sounds and the -lak indirect object.
Taa marbuta after ر is a. An evening sitting with family or friends, from sihir, to stay up late.
ح is 7 and the taa marbuta after م is e. The default sense in Ramallah is red meat, usually lamb or beef.
A form II verb coined from English save, with shadda on ي. I am unsure of the vowel, since sayyif is also heard, and many speakers simply say 3amal save or 7afaTH.
The Palestinian form is Sbaa3 with the first vowel dropped and a long aa, not MSA iSba3. Plural Sawaabi3.
The standard reply to ya3Tiik il-3aafye. The verb drops its first vowel, y3aafiik, and the -k ending is the masculine you.
Although it is a legal term, it is common enough in speech to glottalise: il-'aanoon. In court or news register the same word is said qaanoon.
ط is emphatic T and the final hamza is a glottal stop. Used for a slow internet connection or car; of a person, Palestinians more often say bTii' or thaqiil dam for a different sense.
Both vowels raise to i in Palestinian, zi3il, not MSA za3ila. Covers both hurt feelings and annoyance.
A written-Arabic set phrase that educated Ramallah speakers do use, with shadda on ض and ن as a sun letter. In relaxed speech it would be mahma kaan or 3ala kull 7aal.
Long ee then long oo, leemoon, written with kasra on the ي. The collective; one lemon is leemoone.
One syllable, no helping vowel needed. Same in Palestinian as in MSA.
In the construct nahr keeps its cluster. The hamza is no longer word-initial after the article, so it is written: il-'urdun.
ظ is the emphatic TH. Used in conversation both for great news and as praise of a person.
An older loan heard mainly from the previous generation, and some speakers say varanda with a v. In Ramallah today balkoon is the usual word for the same thing.
Word-initial alif madda is written as the bare long vowel. Urban Palestinian turns ذ into d, so it is respelled آدار; a newsreader would say aadhaar.
س is a sun letter, so is-sane. The relative illi plus the feminine past faatat is the Palestinian way to say last year.
3ala reduces to 3a and fuses with the article. The hamza is medial once the article is attached, so it is written.
kibir with both vowels as i, plus raas and the masculine possessive -u, spelled راسو. A fixed idiom for getting a big head.
